primary_source: Actual crates.io SQLx 0.9.0 source resolved by the frozen workspace lockfile
findings: PoolInner::close marks the pool closed, acquires all connection permits, awaits each raw connection close, then resets counts.
SqliteConnection::close requests worker shutdown, drops its handle, then awaits the worker response.
Command::Shutdown drops connection/shared worker state before sending the completion response.
This provides a concrete wait edge for close-time SQLite work; dropping an external store without awaiting pool close lacks that completion edge.
The wrapper does not grant recovery authority or drop the guard. Recovery must still check every retained file identity and the independently retained current witness.
limits: Awaiting pool closure does not certify unrelated external filesystem writers, make close errors into recovery authorization, or add a non-Unix descriptor backend.
